transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Well, what brings me in is... I just keep having these moments lately where things don't feel right. My own house, or even my office, it just feels completely unreal to me. It's hard to explain, but it's almost like... like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. It's been happening enough that I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.

When these moments of feeling unreal happen, do they come along with a sudden wave of intense fear, racing heart, shortness of breath, or other physical sensations—or do they occur on their own without that kind of surge?

No, I haven't really noticed any of that. My heart doesn't race, and I don't feel short of breath. It's not really a big wave of fear hitting me. 

They just kind of... happen on their own. I'll just be sitting at my desk, maybe looking over a client's tax file, and suddenly I just feel totally disconnected from everything. But physically, no, I don't get those intense sensations you mentioned.
Before these episodes started, did you experience any particularly stressful or traumatic event—like an accident, loss, or frightening situation?

Yeah, actually. This has all been going on for about two weeks now. It started right after... well, I had a situation at work. A client got very upset and he actually threatened me right there in my office. Ever since that happened, about two weeks ago, I've been having these episodes.
Since that incident, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened with that client?

No, not really. I mean, I remember it happened, obviously, but I'm not having nightmares about it or anything like that. And I don't feel like I'm reliving it during the day. It's just that weird, disconnected feeling I mentioned.
Since the incident with that client, have you found yourself avoiding anything that reminds you of it—like avoiding that client, similar situations, or even going into your office?

No, I haven't really been avoiding anything. I still go into the office every day, sit at the same desk. I mean, I haven't seen that specific client again, but I haven't been going out of my way to avoid him or anything else related to work. I just go about my day, doing my job like normal... well, except for those disconnected moments. But no, no avoiding things.

latest_inference.note: Absence of flashbacks, nightmares, or avoidance behaviors argues against acute stress reaction (F43.0) or PTSD. The isolated, recurrent derealization/depersonalization episodes without autonomic arousal or full dissociative amnesia point most consistently to depersonalization-derealization disorder (F48.1).
